description:
FILED s530c (Opus agent, 2026-10-31).  PRE-EXISTING (base 0fb05a79 gives the same).  Found when #3859 let Pod-Simple t/fcodes_s.t run past its old stop: its rows 13-34 (Pod::Simple::Text output) now RUN and fail on this.

    use Text::Wrap; local $Text::Wrap::huge = 'overflow';
    my $o = Text::Wrap::wrap("  ", "  ", "abc
"); $o =~ s/
/\n/g; print "[$o]
";
  perl 5.40.3: [  abc
]        PCL: [  abc]          (also "abc def
ghi
" -> PCL drops the LAST newline only)
Probe scratch/s530c/pr/wrap1.pl.  Pod::Simple::Text::emit_par is `wrap($indent, $indent, $self->{'Thispara'} .= "
")` + print "
", so every paragraph ends "
" where perl's ends "

".

NARROWED (scratch/s530c/pr/wrap2-4.pl, all IDENTICAL to perl): the two regexes of wrap()'s loop with their captures and pos, the loop itself replicated in a script (`while ($t !~ /\G(?:$break)*\Z/gc) {...} $r .= $remainder` gives "  abc
" under PCL too), Text::Tabs::expand("abc
"), the map/join that builds $t.  So the difference is in what the transpiled core Text/Wrap.pm does that the replica does not: candidates `use re 'taint'` in the sub, the `local $Text::Wrap::huge` read through the package global, `$lead`/`$nl` initialisation, or the `pos($t) ne length($t)` tail.  Next step: transpile Text/Wrap.pm (`./pl2cl --module`) and bisect by copying wrap() into a script.
ROWS: Pod-Simple-3.47 t/fcodes_s.t rows 13-34 (22 rows, blessed to this task by s530c).
subject: Text::Wrap::wrap drops the LAST trailing newline of its text (`wrap("  ","  ","abc\n")` is "  abc" where perl gives "  abc\n") -- silent wrong; every Pod::Simple::Text paragraph ends one newline short (Pod-Simple fcodes_s.t rows 13-34)
